Restamp 9 pages re-dated by the pull request 269 squash (#288)

Set the modified date of the 9 pages that pull request 269 stamped
2026-11-13 to 2026-11-22, the day its squash merge landed on main, in
site-src/site.json: home, standard, examples, patterns,
install-other-ai, verify, channels, checklist and disclosure.
Regenerate the 9 pages with tools/build-site.py and the sitemap with
tools/generate-sitemap.py --write, never by hand. Each page changes in
2 generated lines, the article:modified_time meta tag and the JSON-LD
dateModified, and site/sitemap.xml changes in the 9 matching lastmod
values. No other file changes.

The page metadata gate dates each page by its last commit on main, so
the squash moved the 9 pages 9 days past their stamps, beyond the
7-day tolerance of tools/check-page-metadata.py. On the pull request
the gate dated each page by the branch's own commits, so it passed
there. The gate, its tolerance and every test fixture stay as they
are, because the fault is in the stamps.

If this change lands after 2026-11-29, the new stamps fail the same
way; restamp to the landing day and regenerate before merging.
Preventing the class, a pull request whose stamps are more than 7 days
older than its landing day, is left to a separate TODO entry.
